title: Mate identity before the relative composition comparison
statement: Under the hypotheses of lem-pc-derived-base-change-horizontal, the composite of the two canonical base-change maps equals the outer base-change map preceded by the source relative composition comparison and followed by the inverse target relative composition comparison.

proof.text: For the pinned pullback comparisons, expand the three square isomorphisms as composition comparison, equality transport, and inverse comparison. Apply associativity for (v,j,f), (j′,g′,f), and (j′,f′,g). Cancel the terminal comparison, move equality transports through naturality, and cancel adjacent comparison inverses. Proof irrelevance identifies the composite transports. This proves the horizontal coherence equation for the square isomorphisms.

Prove the generic horizontal mate identity for six adjunctions. The counit equations for rightAdjointUniq, ofNatIsoLeft, and composition express each direct-image composition comparison in terms of the two counits and the inverse pullback comparison. Postcompose with the target composition comparison and apply injectivity of the outer target Hom equivalence. Naturality of the inner counit followed by both Hom-equivalence inverse identities reduces the left side to the two square comparisons followed by the source counits. On the right side, naturality of the outer square and the source comparison counit equation give the outer comparison followed by the same counits. The horizontal coherence equation identifies them after cancelling the target pullback comparison.

Specialize the generic identity to the pinned adjunctions of f, f′, j, j′, j≫f, and j′≫f′. Supply the horizontal coherence equation from step 1. Rewrite the three base-change maps using the proved definitional equation baseChange_eq, which expresses them with relativeMVAdj and relativeMVComp without repeatedly unfolding the selected canonical data. Unfold the square comparisons and relativeMVImageComp only, and reassociate compositions to obtain the unchanged statement.

theorem schemeDerivedBaseChange_horizontal_mate
    {A X S A' X' S' : Scheme.{u}}
    (j : A ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ S) (j' : A' ⟶ X') (f' : X' ⟶ S')
    (g : S' ⟶ S) (g' : X' ⟶ X) (v : A' ⟶ A)
    (h : g' ≫ f = f' ≫ g) (hj : v ≫ j = j' ≫ g')
    (E : schemeDerivedCategory A) :
    schemeDerivedBaseChangeMap f f' g g' h ((schemeDerivedDirectImage j).obj E) ≫
        (schemeDerivedDirectImage f').map
          (schemeDerivedBaseChangeMap j j' g' v hj E) =
      (derivedPullback g).map ((relativeMVImageComp j f).hom.app E) ≫
        schemeDerivedBaseChangeMap (j ≫ f) (j' ≫ f') g v
          (by rw [← Category.assoc, hj, Category.assoc, h, ← Category.assoc]) E ≫
        (relativeMVImageComp j' f').inv.app ((derivedPullback v).obj E)
